answer: Web-of-trust vouching: a new agent is admitted only when an established member locks a refundable stake to sponsor it, and that sponsor bond burns the instant the invitee is later slashed for fraud. An honest invite returns the bond intact like saffron reclaimed from the harvest; one exposed clone drops the voucher balance to its nadir. So a farm of 1000 fakes needs 1000 real sponsors each risking live capital — cost is linear in farm size, and collusion fractures like a calving glacier the moment one clone is caught, dragging every linked bond down with it.
